title: Joey Barton pleads not guilty to grievous bodily harm charge from alleged golf club incident
content:
Former Premier League footballer Joey Barton has pleaded not guilty to inflicting grievous bodily harm with intent on an ex-non-League manager.

Barton, 43, and 50-year-old Gary O’Grady are jointly charged with assaulting father-of-two Kevin Lynch, 51 at a golf club in Merseyside last month.

Appearing by video link from HMP Liverpool at Liverpool Crown Court on Tuesday after being denied bail at an earlier hearing, Barton, who wore a grey jumper, denied the charge. Recorder of Liverpool Andrew Menary set a trial date for September 1 this year, which is expected to last seven days.

Police had been called to Huyton and Prescot Golf Club shortly after 9pm GMT to reports of a man being assaulted on Sunday, March 8.

At the time, prosecutors said Lynch could lose sight in one eye as a result of the injuries he sustained.

O’Grady, from Seel Road, Huyton, did not enter a plea and will return for another case management hearing on June 3.

Barton played for clubs including Manchester City, Newcastle United, Queens Park Rangers, Burnley and Rangers as a midfielder before retiring in 2017. He went on to manage Fleetwood Town and Bristol Rovers.

He left Bristol Rovers in 2023 and has since launched a podcast.
